hypothesis: One shared learned refinement operator can invert a coarse functional-harmony skeleton (chords on a strided pillar grid) into a finer per-bar progression, held fixed at the pillars, better than copy/n-gram baselines at the coarse refinement steps where genuine harmonic motion must be produced.

representation.note: Inversions and figured-bass digits are collapsed (V7->V, ii65->ii); they belong to a finer ladder level. Tokens are key-relative so held-out composers share the vocabulary.

splits.composer_holdout: frozen dataset splits: train Mozart 41 + Tchaikovsky 6, validate Dvorak 9, test Beethoven 9 (cross-composer)
splits.movement_holdout: every composer appears in train; one movement per composer held out for validation and test (seen-composer, unseen-movement)

honesty: Exact-match at fine strides is dominated by harmonic persistence; copy_nearest_pillar is the mandatory strong baseline.
This tests one harmonic ladder level only; it is not a full-score composer, a critic, a selection policy, or an RL reward.
Only four composers carry harmonic-function annotations, so cross-composer generalization is measured but expected to be data-limited.
